codeReview.summary: The feature adds the requested retry/backoff structure and solid coverage for 5xx/429 vs. 4xx cases, but the retry classifier is still broader than the contract: it retries every non-HTTP exception instead of only transient network failures.

issues.description: `isRetryable()` falls through to `return true` for every non-`ConvexHttpError`. Because the surrounding `try/catch` also wraps `resp.json()` and any other local exceptions inside the request block (`server/shared/convexClient.ts:159-170`), malformed 2xx JSON bodies or request-construction errors will be retried even though the feature only allows retries for network errors, HTTP 5xx, and 429. The retry policy is therefore broader than specified.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The shared command inventory still has no dedicated server unit-test command even though server-side `node:test` coverage now exists.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `.factory/services.yaml` defines `build_server` but no `test_server`; `server/package.json` only exposes `build`, `dev`, and `start`; the worker transcript shows extra discovery work (reading `server/package.json` and existing `*.test.ts` files) before it could run `node --import tsx --test shared/convexClient.test.ts`.

sharedStateObservations.observation: `refactor-worker`'s documented red-phase procedure is not being enforced consistently in worker feedback.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `.factory/skills/refactor-worker/SKILL.md` Step 3 says new functionality should get failing tests first, but the transcript shows `Edit` on `server/shared/convexClient.ts` before `Create` of `server/shared/convexClient.test.ts`, while the handoff still reports `skillFeedback.followedProcedure: true`.

summary: Reviewed the feature metadata, handoff, transcript skeleton, skill file, and commit `342ffbb` for `reliability-server-convex-retry`. The review fails because the implementation retries arbitrary non-HTTP exceptions, so it does not yet match the requested retry policy of only network errors, HTTP 5xx, and 429.
